concepts.name: VSEPR Theory, Hybridization & Molecular Geometry
concepts.summary: VSEPR theory: Repulsion order: $\text{lp-lp} > \text{lp-bp} > \text{bp-bp}$. Hybridization steric number $H = \frac{1}{2}[V + M - C + A]$. $\text{SF}_4$: $sp^3d$, 1 lp, see-saw. $\text{ClF}_3$: $sp^3d$, 2 lp, T-shaped. $\text{XeF}_2$: $sp^3d$, 3 lp, linear. $\text{XeF}_4$: $sp^3d^2$, 2 lp, square planar. $\text{PCl}_5$: $sp^3d$, trigonal bipyramidal (axial bonds are longer and weaker than equatorial bonds).
concepts.standard_formulas: \text{Steric Number } = \text{Bond Pairs} + \text{Lone Pairs}, \quad H = \frac{1}{2}(V + M - C + A)
concepts.common_traps: In $\text{PCl}_5$, the 2 axial $\text{P-Cl}$ bonds are longer and weaker than the 3 equatorial bonds due to greater repulsion from equatorial electron pairs.
concepts.tips_and_tricks: In $sp^3d$ hybridization, lone pairs ALWAYS occupy EQUATORIAL positions to minimize $90^\circ$ repulsions (e.g. $\text{ClF}_3$ has both lone pairs in equatorial positions $\implies$ T-shape).

concepts.name: Molecular Orbital Theory & Dipole Moments
concepts.summary: MOT: Bond Order $= \frac{N_b - N_a}{2}$. For $\le 14$ electrons ($\text{B}_2, \text{C}_2, \text{N}_2$): $\pi 2p_x = \pi 2p_y$ fills before $\sigma 2p_z$. For $> 14$ electrons ($\text{O}_2, \text{F}_2$): $\sigma 2p_z$ fills before $\pi 2p$. $\text{O}_2$ has 2 unpaired electrons in degenerate antibonding $\pi^* 2p$ orbitals $\implies$ paramagnetic with $\text{Bond Order} = 2$. Dipole moment $\mu = q \times d$; symmetrical molecules ($\text{CO}_2, \text{BF}_3, \text{CCl}_4$) have $\mu = 0$.
concepts.common_traps: Liquid $\text{O}_2$ is attracted into a magnetic field because it is PARAMAGNETIC (a fact that Valence Bond Theory completely failed to explain, but MOT successfully explains).
concepts.tips_and_tricks: If Bond Order $= 0$, the diatomic molecule does not exist (e.g. $\text{He}_2, \text{Be}_2$).

### 2.1 VSEPR Theory, Hybridization & Molecular Geometry (Molecular Geometry)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **17 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: VSEPR theory: Repulsion order: $\text{lp-lp} > \text{lp-bp} > \text{bp-bp}$. Hybridization steric number $H = \frac{1}{2}[V + M - C + A]$. $\text{SF}_4$: $sp^3d$, 1 lp, see-saw. $\text{ClF}_3$: $sp^3d$, 2 lp, T-shaped. $\text{XeF}_2$: $sp^3d$, 3 lp, linear. $\text{XeF}_4$: $sp^3d^2$, 2 lp, square planar. $\text{PCl}_5$: $sp^3d$, trigonal bipyramidal (axial bonds are longer and weaker than equatorial bonds).

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Steric Number } = \text{Bond Pairs} + \text{Lone Pairs}, \quad H = \frac{1}{2}(V + M - C + A)
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: In $\text{PCl}_5$, the 2 axial $\text{P-Cl}$ bonds are longer and weaker than the 3 equatorial bonds due to greater repulsion from equatorial electron pairs.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: In $sp^3d$ hybridization, lone pairs ALWAYS occupy EQUATORIAL positions to minimize $90^\circ$ repulsions (e.g. $\text{ClF}_3$ has both lone pairs in equatorial positions $\implies$ T-shape).

- **[2021 Shift] Q#3 (MCQ)**: *"Which of the following is an incorrect statement?..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.2 Molecular Orbital Theory & Dipole Moments (Bonding Theories)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **9 PYQs** (High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: MOT: Bond Order $= \frac{N_b - N_a}{2}$. For $\le 14$ electrons ($	ext{B}_2, 	ext{C}_2, 	ext{N}_2$): $\pi 2p_x = \pi 2p_y$ fills before $\sigma 2p_z$. For $> 14$ electrons ($	ext{O}_2, 	ext{F}_2$): $\sigma 2p_z$ fills before $\pi 2p$. $\text{O}_2$ has 2 unpaired electrons in degenerate antibonding $\pi^* 2p$ orbitals $\implies$ paramagnetic with $\text{Bond Order} = 2$. Dipole moment $\mu = q \times d$; symmetrical molecules ($	ext{CO}_2, \text{BF}_3, \text{CCl}_4$) have $\mu = 0$.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Bond Order} = \frac{N_b - N_a}{2}, \quad \text{Bond Order} \propto \text{Bond Energy} \propto \frac{1}{\text{Bond Length}}
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Liquid $\text{O}_2$ is attracted into a magnetic field because it is PARAMAGNETIC (a fact that Valence Bond Theory completely failed to explain, but MOT successfully explains).

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: If Bond Order $= 0$, the diatomic molecule does not exist (e.g. $\text{He}_2, \text{Be}_2$).

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring KCET Pitfalls in Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure

### 1. Speed & 80-Second Constraint Management
KCET demands answering 60 questions in 80 minutes (~1.33 minutes per question). The most lethal trap is spending 3+ minutes on long algebraic derivations. Always check for dimensional consistency or option substitution first.

### 2. NCERT & Karnataka PU Board Direct Lines
Over 45% of KCET theory questions are taken directly from NCERT / Karnataka PU Board textbook summary points, margins, and standard exemplar questions. Pay rigorous attention to exceptions (e.g., electron gain enthalpy of Cl vs F, acidic nature of boric acid, non-polar symmetrical geometries).

### 3. Unit Conversions & Prefix Overlooks
Units of molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), micro/nano multipliers (10^-6, 10^-9), and centimeter-to-meter conversions in optics and gravitation account for the highest frequency of careless mark losses in KCET.

### 4. No Negative Marking Advantage
Since KCET has NO negative marking, never leave any question unattempted. When down to two options, use dimensional elimination or parity checks to maximize expected score.
